focus: Audit sample, label provenance, and call cost; design a trustworthy benchmark
noveltyJustification: The declared committed corpus cannot meet the gate, while the measured authored fixture has different provenance and population; call-level cost is measurable but live spend is not.
keyQuestions: How can accuracy improve or cost fall?
What would make the measurement trustworthy?
answeredQuestions: Replay proof, explicit label adjudication, class/hub metrics, held-out evaluation, and live-volume measurement are needed.

label: The 54-row fixture changes the planned corpus: feature 020 found 2 committed clarifications and zero gold among 359 prompts, below its 30-label gate.
The score gate validates label membership but not compiled-router replay or label approval provenance; operator=54 counts labels, not operator identity.
Accuracy should separate valid named-mode selection from none_of_these abstention and report by hub/class with false-default rate and held-out evaluation.
The benchmark used 163 measured calls, 19446 estimated input tokens, 327.5ms median and 380ms nearest-rank p95 choice-call latency; no actual dollars or live volume are available.
A single randomized choice per eligible live clarify could reduce choice calls, but its accuracy/stability versus three rotations is unvalidated and must be tested on held-out rows.

direction: Treat estimated input tokens and call wall time as actual spend or production latency
reason: The logs lack billing/token-usage fields and the prompt spec says real clarify rate was not measured.
